name: Stormvein Dynamics Pelagic-6 Aquatic Leg
product_name: Stormvein Dynamics Pelagic-6 Aquatic Leg System
description:
The Pelagic-6 is a full leg replacement purpose-built for aquatic and extreme-wet environments, featuring hydrodynamically contoured limb housings that reduce drag by 38% compared to standard prosthetics in water. The foot assembly deploys integrated composite swim fins via a neural-triggered rotary mechanism, folding flat for terrestrial walking within 1.2 seconds of signal. Pressure compensation bladders in the knee and hip joints automatically equalize to ambient water pressure, preventing joint deformation and seal failure to a rated depth of 80 meters. The entire system is sealed to IP68 with corrosion-resistant titanium hardware and anti-biofouling polymer coating on all external surfaces.

The Pelagic-6 is used by Great Lakes harbor workers, underwater infrastructure maintenance crews, and the small but passionate community of competitive aquatic athletes who race in the lake's open-water circuits. The design is also popular with the fishing communities on the lake's outer islands, where the ability to work effectively in the water is simply a survival skill. Stormvein maintains a service depot on the lakefront specifically because saltwater-adjacent environments demand regular anti-fouling treatment.
installation_requirements: Certified prosthetist with aquatic-systems endorsement, bilateral installation mandatory, pressure calibration dive required post-installation
rejection_risk: Low — Lazarus-licensed biocompatible socket coating, pressure equalization prevents joint stress that drives rejection in suboptimal aquatic prosthetics
maintenance: Anti-biofouling recoat every 6 months; fin mechanism lubrication monthly; pressure bladder integrity check every 3 months; full seal inspection annually

side_effects: Hydrodynamic limb profile adds visible bulk at thigh and calf, making standard clothing fit poorly and identifying the user's hardware to observers
Fin deployment mechanism occasionally triggers partially during rapid dorsiflexion on land, causing tripping hazard
Pressure compensation bladders create audible gurgling sensation during rapid elevation changes such as elevator rides
Anti-biofouling coating has a faint chemical smell noticeable in enclosed spaces that users become nose-blind to
cultural_context: The Pelagic-6 is visually distinct in ways that mark its wearers as people whose lives touch the water — harbor workers, lake racers, island community members. In the interior districts it reads as exotic, even romantic. Stormvein has leaned into this, and the Pelagic-6 has a modest fashion following among Tier 3-4 lakefront residents who want the aesthetic without the professional need.

Outer island fishing and maritime communities
story_hooks: A Pelagic-6 wearer surfaced from a dive reporting they found a sealed structure at 60 meters that doesn't appear on any municipal infrastructure map — and someone tried to kill them before they could file a report

Stormvein's anti-biofouling coating formula has been quietly changed, and users who serviced recently are experiencing accelerated corrosion at the joint seals — the old formula used a compound that's now controlled
An underwater racing circuit has been disqualified en masse after officials ruled that Pelagic-6 fins constitute a prohibited propulsion assist — Stormvein is funding the legal appeal
